- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.5) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for volatility.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast for 2–3 periods.  
- If model consistently forecasts below true outcome in early periods (e.g., 1–3 days ahead), it may be underestimating mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (e.g., alternating +/–0.5+), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecasts by averaging last 3–5 price points before prediction.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently lower than forecast, model may be overconfident; apply a 1–2% downward bias to next 30-day forecast.
